property_summary: After cancelProposal, the ratio of total votes cast to the number of proposals created remains between 0 and 1 when considering the old proposal ID was finalising and new proposal ID has minority.
After any sequence of public calls ending with cancelProposal, the proposalCount must be greater than or equal to zero.
After calling cancelProposal, the value returned by proposalCount() must be strictly greater than before the call when the cancelProposal is preceded by a newAddressProposal call.
After calling cancelProposal on a finalising proposal and a new proposal of the same type, the proposalCount must increase by exactly one.
After a successful cancelProposal call, the proposalCount must be strictly greater than before the call.
After a cancelProposal call, the VADER address should remain unchanged from the value set during init.
After cancelProposal, the VADER address in the contract equals the first argument passed to init (_vader), regardless of any calls made.
After calling cancelProposal, the stored VADER address equals the _vader parameter from init, regardless of any other calls.
After any sequence of public calls ending with cancelProposal, the VADER address stored in the contract equals the first argument passed to the init function.
After cancelProposal, VADER address equals _vader parameter from init, unaffected by cancelProposal calls.
After init, the value of USDV should always equal the second argument passed to init, regardless of subsequent calls to cancelProposal.
After calling cancelProposal, the value of c.USDV() should remain unchanged from its state before the call.
After a cancelProposal call, the USDV address remains the one set during init, regardless of the proposal arguments.
After a cancelProposal call, the USDV address remains unchanged from its initial value set during init.
USDV address remains equal to the original _usdv parameter passed to init after any cancelProposal call.
The USDV address is not changed by cancelProposal() calls.
The USDV address set during init remains invariant across all cancelProposal calls.
After calling cancelProposal, the USDV variable must equal the initial usdv parameter passed to init, not the vault address.
After cancelProposal, the USDV address must be different from the VAULT address.
After cancelProposal, the USDV contract address must equal the USDV parameter passed in init, not the vault address.
The USDV address after cancelProposal equals the USDV parameter from init, not the vault address.
The value of USDV returned by the public getter remains constant across multiple calls to cancelProposal, whereas the bug causes it to change.
After any call to cancelProposal, the VAULT address must not be changed to address(0) when the proposal was finalising.
After cancelProposal completes, the VAULT address in the contract must equal the _vault address passed during init.
After any call to cancelProposal, the contract's VAULT address must not be address(0).
After init, VAULT always equals _vault passed as argument.
After cancelProposal completes, the VAULT address must be the original _vault address passed during init, unless it was never initialized (inited false).
After cancelProposal, coolOffPeriod remains unchanged from its initial value (1).
After any sequence of operations culminating in cancelProposal, the sum of votes for the old and new proposals does not exceed the total weight of the vault.
After calling cancelProposal, the current timestamp minus the finalisation start time of the old proposal is not less than the coolOffPeriod (unless it was exactly set to 0).
After cancelProposal returns successfully, the finalising state of the old proposal is reset to false (or the proposal is marked as not finalising).
After cancelProposal is called, mapPID_votes[oldProposalID] must be zero.
After cancelProposal(oldProposalID, newProposalID) is called, the votes of oldProposalID must be zero when read via the public getter.

After cancelProposal(oldProposalID, newProposalID) is called, the total supply of votes for oldProposalID must decrease by at most the vote weight of the caller that was previously assigned to the proposal.
After cancelProposal(oldProposalID, newProposalID) is called, mapPID_votes[oldProposalID] must be less than the total votes before the cancel (i.e., it must have decreased).

After cancelProposal(oldProposalID, newProposalID) is called, the sum of mapPID_votes[oldProposalID] and mapPID_votes[newProposalID] must equal the sum of mapPIDMember_votes[oldProposalID][any] over all members plus the corresponding sum for newProposalID, which is impossible to check externally; instead, after cancelProposal, mapPID_votes[oldProposalID] must be less than the total weight to ensure it cannot be used for quorum again.
